::: {.callout-note}
## Unreleased

This API is being developed on `dev/schema-inference`. It is not part of the package
version currently pinned by this documentation checkout.
:::

`rf.infer(data, ...)` drafts field definitions from a data module's bounded
sample of preprocessed training observations. Configure the data and its
preprocessors first, review the draft, then build and fit an ordinary model.

Inference can identify a Boolean or numeric column and the structure of
repeated records. You still choose the prediction target and the meaning of
identifiers, labels, dates, and ordered collections.

## Prepare the data module first

Suppose your Parquet files contain `amount_minor`, `merchant`, and Boolean
`disputed` columns. A module-owned preprocessor converts the amount into
major units, producing records such as:

```yaml
amount: 42.50
merchant: corner_market
disputed: false
```

Create the module without a model, then infer from its processed training
records. Declare the target and choose an open vocabulary for merchant labels:

```python
import polars as pl
import relflow as rf

@rf.preprocess
def prepare(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return frame.with_columns(
        amount=pl.col("amount_minor") / 100,
    ).drop("amount_minor")

data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    train="payments/raw/train.parquet",
    validate="payments/raw/validation.parquet",
    preprocessor=prepare,
)
proposal = rf.infer(
    data,
    targets=["/disputed"],
    overrides={"/merchant": rf.Category},
)
print(proposal.report)

model = rf.Model.xs(fields=proposal.fields)
model.fit(data, batch_size=128, max_epochs=20)
```

`disputed` becomes `rf.Boolean(mask=True)`, keeping the target out of the
model input. Fitting binds the previously unbound module to this model and
opens a fresh training pass using the same preprocessor. Inference never
requests validation or test data.

The data module owns sources and preprocessing. Pass the module to `rf.infer`;
raw sources and a separate inference `preprocessor=` argument are not supported.

```{typst}
//| label: fig-inferred-payment
//| fig-cap: "Inference examines the module’s processed training records and drafts this ordinary model tree."
//| fig-alt: "The module preprocesses amount_minor into Number amount before inference. The proposed payment tree contains amount, explicit Category merchant, and Boolean disputed. Disputed is hidden from input and used as the target."
#tree(node("payment", kind: "root", children: (
  node("amount", type: "Number", body: [
    Prepared from #raw("amount_minor").
  ]),
  node("merchant", type: "Category", body: [
    Chosen explicitly.
  ]),
  node("disputed", kind: "target", type: "Boolean", body: [
    Always hidden from input.
  ]),
)))
```

`rf.Inference` is a configuration proposal. Profiling does not initialize a
model, download a text encoder, learn a vocabulary, or fit a normalizer.
Omitting `targets` drafts inputs without inventing a training objective.

## Resolve the decisions

`proposal.report` records physical types, sampled statistics, candidate types,
reasons, exclusions, and sampling limits. It contains aggregate evidence rather
than source text bodies. It remains available when some fields are unresolved.

`proposal.unresolved` lists those addresses. Accessing `proposal.fields` raises
until every included field has a decision; unresolved columns never disappear
silently. Each successful access returns fresh field definitions.

For a richer dataset, configure another module and concentrate the modeling
choices in overrides:

```python
data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    train="payments/enriched/train.parquet",
    validate="payments/enriched/validation.parquet",
)
proposal = rf.infer(
    data,
    targets=["/disputed"],
    overrides={
        "/merchant": rf.Category,
        "/description": rf.Text(max_length=64),
        "/recent_transactions": {"length": 64, "overflow": "tail"},
        "/recent_transactions/merchant": rf.Category,
        "/raw_payload": None,
    },
)
```

Here `recent_transactions` contains `days_ago`, `amount`, and `merchant`
fields, ordered oldest to newest and known before the current payment.
The explicit cap retains the last 64 records. `None` excludes `raw_payload`
and records that exclusion.

A field class or configured request chooses its datatype. An options mapping
patches a uniquely inferred leaf or an inferred branch while preserving its
children. A mapping cannot choose between competing datatypes. Unknown
addresses, undeclared options, incompatible shapes, and masks conflicting
with `targets` raise errors.

Targets are absolute leaf addresses. Numeric codes such as `0` and `1` do not
silently become Boolean: choose numeric prediction or classification, and
preprocess a cast if Boolean input is intended. Text targets require an
explicit choice because `Text` reconstructs embeddings rather than generating
strings. `DateParts` likewise does not decode a complete timestamp.

## What the draft can infer

| Training column | Initial decision |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean scalar | `Boolean` |
| Integer or floating scalar | `Number` for inputs; low-cardinality targets need a task choice. |
| Repeated short strings | `Category` when sufficient low-cardinality evidence is available. |
| Prose-like strings | `Text` when the length or word-count rule applies. |
| Fixed-size numeric list | `Vector(n_dim=N)` when the declared width is positive and sampled elements contain no inner nulls. |
| List of objects | A `Branch`, with its children inferred recursively. |
| Dates, ambiguous strings, primitive lists, or unsupported types | Pending until you choose a compatible representation, preprocess, or exclude them. |

The initial Category rule requires at least 256 non-null strings, at most
64 observed distinct values, a distinct fraction no greater than 0.2, and a
95th-percentile length no greater than 64 characters. Text requires a median
length of at least 64 characters or a median of at least eight
whitespace-delimited words. If both rules apply, choose explicitly.
These are reported heuristics, not guarantees about the complete dataset.

Dictionary encoding does not establish a closed enum domain. Inference never
chooses `Enum` from sample uniques, or infers identifier and unordered-set
semantics from cardinality alone. Plain nested objects need preprocessing or
an explicit extension; they do not become singleton branches. A variable-length
primitive list does not acquire a vector dimension because sampled lengths
happen to match.

Variable-length object collections produce unbounded branches. Their sampled
maximum is not a learned hard limit. Before public serving, set explicit
branch limits and request-size limits: untrusted collection lengths can exhaust
memory or compute and present a DoS/DDoS attack vector. See
[Branch limits](../data-types/branch.qmd#automatic-lengths-and-limits).

## Chunks, preprocessing, and limits

Configure Arrow tables, record batches, datasets, file paths, `rf.source(...)`,
or restartable factories on the data module. For example, an application-owned
Arrow dataset can expose smaller raw training chunks:

```python
def training_chunks():
    return dataset.scanner(batch_size=4096).to_reader()

data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    train=training_chunks,
    preprocessor=prepare,
)
proposal = rf.infer(
    data,
    targets=["/disputed"],
    overrides={"/merchant": rf.Category},
    max_rows=10_000,
    max_batches=8,
    max_bytes=64 * 1024**2,
    max_values=1_000_000,
)
```

`dataset` above is an application-supplied `pyarrow.dataset.Dataset` containing
only raw training observations. A bare one-shot iterator, reader, or configured
scanner is rejected; wrap it in a factory that recreates it, or materialize it
deliberately. The module applies `prepare` before profiling those chunks.

Profiling reads a deterministic prefix and stops at the first budget reached.
Row and byte budgets apply independently before and after preprocessing;
`max_values` also bounds nested terminal values. Empty chunks count against
the batch budget. The report identifies budget termination and prefix bias.
Changing chunk sizes can change the sample when the batch limit is active.

These bounds limit profiling work. They do not bound backend I/O, retained
Arrow buffers, process memory, or arbitrary preprocessing allocations.
Owned readers and generators are closed when sampling finishes or fails.

Scalar dictionary encoding is supported. Nested or non-scalar dictionary values,
Arrow list-view and large-list-view arrays, and run-end-encoded arrays are
rejected before profiling because bounded traversal does not support those
containers. Decode them or convert them to ordinary Arrow arrays before
profiling; they do not produce pending datatype proposals.

Configure preprocessing once on the module. Its training pipeline runs before
profiling, and fitting uses that same pipeline on fresh observations. Only
partition preprocessors that need neither a model schema nor encoding context
are supported by bounded profiling. Dataset-wide joins or aggregations must
produce an already-prepared source first; profiling a prefix would change their
meaning. See [Preprocessing](preprocessors.qmd).

`ArrowDataModule`, `PolarsDataModule`, `DuckDBDataModule`,
`SyntheticDataModule`, and `CustomDataModule` can be configured before a model.
Already-bound modules also support inference. Third-party modules implement
`rf.InferenceData`: their `profile(...)` method accepts the sampling budgets
and returns a `relflow.data.profiling.Sample` from canonical training
observations after their own preprocessing. Inference does not discover data
through tensor loaders. See [Data Modules](data-modules.qmd).

## Keep the reviewed schema

Use `proposal.fields` through existing
[model presets](../reference/model-presets.qmd), or freeze the configuration
through canonical Schema JSON:

```python
schema = rf.Schema.from_tree(
    d_model=64,
    n_layers=1,
    n_heads=2,
    fields=proposal.fields,
)
saved = schema.model_dump_json()
restored = rf.Schema.model_validate_json(saved)
model = rf.Model(schema=restored)
```

New data chunks do not mutate those decisions. A schema revision requires a
new proposal and ordinary model construction or
[schema mutation](schema-mutation.qmd).

An unbound module can be profiled but cannot create tensor loaders. The model's
loop methods bind it automatically; binding a module that already belongs to a
different model raises an error. The proposal itself does not bind the module
or create encoding context.

Custom datatypes can opt into `rf.Component.infer` using a bounded `rf.Profile`
and return `rf.Proposal(request, reason)`, a pending proposal with
`request=None`, or no proposal. The optional `request` argument lets the hook
validate an explicit override. Hooks are read from the live registry;
competing proposals require a user choice. See
[Custom Tensorfields](custom-tensorfields.qmd) for extension ownership.
